name: How do contractors install built-in shelving in older Denver homes with uneven walls?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors install built-in shelving in older Denver homes with uneven walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes across central Denver neighborhoods often feature unlevel hardwood floors, settled framing, and uneven lath-and-plaster walls that require custom scribing and leveling techniques. Standard factory cabinets do not sit flush against bowed historic walls without unsightly gaps. A finish carpenter builds custom face frames and trims individual shelf edges on-site, scribing them to trace the natural curvature of historic plaster. Baseboard trim and crown moldings are blended into the room's original millwork profiles. This hands-on adjustment ensures the newly installed shelving looks like an original architectural feature of the historic home rather than an awkward modern addition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Finish carpenters level the base, scribe face frames to match wavy plaster walls, and custom-cut trim to blend with historic baseboards and crown molding.
